clue.text: High-ranking lady, for instance, is introduced to tramp

indicators.note: something introduced to another thing is put inside it, so one piece goes into the other

blocks.note: a bum is a vagrant or tramp
e.g. is the abbreviation for 'for example'

explanation.surface: A grand lady is presented to a vagrant, as an example of social mixing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tramp' looks like a verb, to walk heavily; it is the noun, a vagrant, in its slang form.
explanation.definitionFit: A begum is a Muslim woman of high rank in South Asia, such as a princess or a nobleman's widow.

clue.text: Wife of man who likes to gamble and drink

blocks.note: a better is someone who places bets
a half is a half-pint of beer, a common pub order

explanation.surface: The long-suffering wife of a gambling drinker.
explanation.walkthrough: In a British pub 'a half' is half a pint of beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Better half is a jocular idiom for one's spouse, usually a husband speaking of his wife.

clue.text: Talk idly, and hang up

indicators.note: in a down entry 'up' means the word is written from bottom to top

blocks.note: to sag is to hang or droop

explanation.surface: Someone chats aimlessly on the phone and then puts the receiver down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hang up' looks like ending a phone call; 'up' is separate, turning the word for droop upward.
explanation.definitionFit: To gas is informal for chattering at length about nothing in particular, the same as idle talk.

clue.text: Silver found in lake in small quantities

indicators.note: a thing found in another sits inside it, so the metal goes within the water

blocks.note: a mere is a lake or pond
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Traces of silver have turned up in a lake, but only a little.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a phrase used like an adjective: a meagre supply comes in small quantities.
explanation.definitionFit: Meagre means scanty or lacking in amount, describing what comes only in small quantities.

clue.text: Disorganised fellow loses head when encountering danger

indicators.note: losing the head means the word drops its first letter

blocks.note: a chap is a man or fellow
a hazard is a danger

explanation.surface: A man meets peril and is beheaded, ending up rather a mess.
explanation.definitionFit: Something haphazard is done without planning or order, so it is the same as disorganised or random.

clue.text: Severity of gear worn by mum!

indicators.note: what is worn by something is wrapped around it, so the one word encloses the other

blocks.note: a harness is gear or tackle, such as a horse's straps
'mum!' is an order to keep quiet, as is sh

explanation.surface: A stern reaction to what Mother is wearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mum' looks like mother; 'mum's the word' means keep silent, so 'mum!' is a call for hush.
explanation.definitionFit: Harshness is the quality of being severe or cruel, so it is a synonym of severity.

clue.text: Two fairies appearing interminably as part of video display

indicators.note: without an end, so each word loses its final letter

blocks.note: first fairy: pixy, a variant spelling of pixie
second fairy: an elf

explanation.surface: A pair of sprites keep showing up endlessly on a television screen.
explanation.walkthrough: The pixy spelling of pixie is needed so that dropping its last letter leaves PIX.
explanation.definitionFit: A pixel is one of the tiny dots of colour that together make up an image on a screen.

clue.text: A doctor (American) he is needed for sudden attacks

blocks.note: taken as written
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's degree
US is short for the United States, hence American
the contraction he's, without its apostrophe

explanation.surface: An American doctor is called in to deal with sudden fits.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambushes are surprise assaults launched from hiding, which makes them sudden attacks.

clue.text: Compare this with change of air

indicators.note: a change of the letters means they are moved round into a fresh order

blocks.note: these eleven letters, rearranged

explanation.surface: Try comparing this place against a holiday in a different climate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change of air' reads as a phrase for a holiday; it splits into the signal and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Atmospheric means relating to the atmosphere, the layer of gases surrounding the earth.

clue.text: 13 animals

indicators.note: the answer to clue 13 begins with the word broken, which instructs us to rearrange the word that follows it

blocks.note: the cross-reference stands for the answer to 13 down, whose second word is the fodder

explanation.walkthrough: 13 down is BROKEN REED, which read as a phrase says break up REED, giving DEER.
explanation.definitionFit: Deer are hoofed ruminant mammals such as stags and does, so they are animals.

clue.text: Artiste unsettled in Texas -she leaves

indicators.note: unsettled letters are disturbed and do not stay in their printed order
the word 'in' places the rearranged letters inside the state's abbreviation

blocks.note: the seven letters of this word, rearranged
TX is the postal abbreviation for the US state

explanation.surface: A performer who has not settled in Texas decides to go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'she leaves' reads like the artiste departing Texas; it means a woman who leaves property in a will.
explanation.definitionFit: A testatrix is a woman who has made a will, so she bequeaths, or leaves, her estate to heirs.

clue.text: Sweet old boy retired with honour

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the abbreviation is written backwards

blocks.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
the MBE (Member of the Order of the British Empire) is a British honour

explanation.surface: A former pupil has retired with a decoration, and it was nice.
explanation.walkthrough: The MBE is an award given in the British honours list.
explanation.definitionFit: A bombe is a frozen dessert moulded into a dome shape, so it is a sweet in the British sense of pudding.

clue.text: Engage in controversy, and appear among best-sellers?

blocks.note: first meaning: join a contest, as a knight entering the tournament ground
second meaning, read literally: get onto the published charts of top-selling books

explanation.surface: An author picks a public fight and lands on the best-seller charts.
explanation.walkthrough: The lists were the fenced ground for a jousting tournament; the question mark flags the punning literal second reading.
explanation.definitionFit: To enter the lists is an idiom for joining a contest or dispute, from knights riding into the jousting arena.

clue.text: Get the bird to peep

blocks.note: first meaning, read literally: obtain a male goose
second meaning: have a quick look

explanation.walkthrough: 'Get the bird' usually means be booed off stage; here it is literal, and a gander is a male goose.
explanation.definitionFit: To take a gander is informal slang for having a look, so it fits a quick peep.

clue.text: Unreliable person, bankrupt, initially really in want

indicators.note: initially means at the beginning, so only the opening letter is kept
'in' puts that first letter inside the word for want

blocks.note: broke means having no money, ruined
want in the sense of lack or need
the first letter of this word

explanation.surface: A ruined man in real need proves to be someone nobody can count on.
explanation.definitionFit: A broken reed is an idiom, from Isaiah, for a person who fails you when you lean on them.

clue.text: Henry joins President for a walk

blocks.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance
Ike was the nickname of US President Dwight Eisenhower

explanation.surface: A man called Henry goes out strolling with the President.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Henry' looks like a king or a first name; here it is the physics unit, symbol H.
explanation.definitionFit: A hike is a long walk, usually through countryside, so the noun matches a walk exactly.

clue.text: Ringleader has to shout love out to the sky

indicators.note: 'love out' tells us the letter standing for nil is removed from the word for shout

blocks.note: to bellow is to shout loudly
love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O
the ether is the upper air or clear sky, in poetic use

explanation.surface: The leader of a gang must yell his passion to the heavens.
explanation.walkthrough: Love is the tennis word for a score of nil; the ether is an old poetic name for the clear upper sky.
explanation.definitionFit: A bellwether is the belled castrated ram that leads a flock, hence a leader whom others follow, here a ringleader.

clue.text: Relating to movement in train and car

blocks.note: a loco is a locomotive, the engine of a train
a motor is a car

explanation.surface: A study of travel by rail and road.
explanation.definitionFit: Locomotor is an adjective describing locomotion, the ability to move from place to place.

clue.text: Agonised? About to identify the problem

indicators.note: turned about means moved around, so the letters of the word before are reordered

blocks.note: these eight letters, rearranged

explanation.surface: A worried patient is in pain, and the doctor is about to work out what is wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: To diagnose is to determine the nature of an illness or fault by examining the signs.

clue.text: Entomological specimen left in case, specially displayed

indicators.note: displayed specially means set out in a new, specially arranged order

blocks.note: these ten letters, rearranged

explanation.surface: A collector leaves a bug in a display case, arranged for show.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface looks like a description of a museum cabinet, which is exactly where such a creature would be.
explanation.definitionFit: A leaf insect is a tropical bug shaped and coloured like a leaf, so it is a fit item for an entomologist's collection.

clue.text: Long journey starts to tire rather excited kids

indicators.note: the starts belonging to the following words means each one's opening letter

blocks.note: the first letters of these four words

explanation.surface: A long trip begins to wear out children who were already overexcited.
explanation.definitionFit: A trek is an arduous journey, often on foot, so it means a long journey.

clue.text: Soldiers reprimanded - what a bloomer

blocks.note: OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers
chid is an old past tense of chide, to scold

explanation.surface: Troops are told off for making a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' looks like a blunder; here it means a plant that blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchid is a showy flowering plant, so it is a bloomer, something that bears blossoms.

clue.text: Wasp, perhaps, disturbing an organic meal

indicators.note: disturbing something throws it into disorder, so these letters are shaken into a new order

blocks.note: these thirteen letters, rearranged

explanation.surface: A wasp buzzes around and spoils a picnic of organic food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wasp' looks like the insect; it is WASP, a White Anglo-Saxon Protestant American.
explanation.definitionFit: A WASP is an American of British descent, so one example of a person with both English and US heritage.

clue.text: Go round and round, then run a little

blocks.note: the letter O is round in shape
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for a run
a bit is a little

explanation.surface: Circle repeatedly, then jog for a short while.
explanation.definitionFit: To orbit is to travel in a curved path around a planet or star, so it means to circle.

clue.text: Reptile caught gigantic bird

blocks.note: c is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
the roc is a giant bird of Arabian legend

explanation.surface: A reptile has snapped up an enormous bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Croc is the informal short form of crocodile, a large reptile of rivers and swamps.

clue.text: Set commercial in South American city

indicators.note: 'in' places the advertisement inside the name of the city

blocks.note: an ad is a commercial or advertisement
Rio de Janeiro in Brazil

explanation.surface: An advertisement is filmed in a city in South America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set' looks like a verb for placing the commercial; it is the noun, a receiving set.
explanation.definitionFit: A radio is a receiving set, the apparatus that picks up broadcasts, just as a TV is a set.

clue.text: Ablutions at Longleat?

blocks.note: surface reading: where washing is done at a stately home
setter's reading: the stately home is the residence of the Marquess of Bath, so it is literally his family seat

explanation.walkthrough: Longleat is a stately home in Wiltshire, seat of the Marquess of Bath; a place for washing is also the house belonging to Bath.
explanation.definitionFit: A bathhouse is a building for bathing, a place for ablutions, and Longleat is the Bath family's house.

clue.text: Wool-producers said to provide such employment

indicators.note: said means spoken, so we go by how the word sounds rather than how it is spelt

blocks.note: female sheep grow wool
link words joining the wordplay to the definition; the letters that run backwards across them are a coincidence

explanation.surface: Sheep are said to keep a whole wool trade employed.
explanation.definitionFit: Use, as a noun, means the act of employing something, so it works as employment.

clue.text: Work to make something of deal, say

definitions.text: Work to make something of deal, say

blocks.clueFragment: Work to make something of deal
blocks.note: surface reading: someone working to make a success of a business agreement
setter's reading: deal is pine or fir timber, so this is a tradesman who builds things from wood

explanation.walkthrough: 'deal' looks like a business agreement; it is sawn softwood such as pine, and 'say' marks it as one example of timber.
explanation.definitionFit: A carpenter is a woodworker whose job is making and fixing wooden items, from planks such as deal.

clue.text: Get right inside without feeling fear

indicators.note: 'Get right inside' says to put the letter for right within the next word

blocks.note: a dead limb is numb, without any feeling
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Someone gets right to the heart of things and feels no fear at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Dread is great fear or apprehension, so the noun swaps directly for fear.
